titulo: Your Return, Your Money, Your Future
intro: Financial well-being program for people returning from the United States to Mexico, whether deported or by their own decision: 8 modules and 24 short lessons. Hybrid format: one in-person kickoff session and the rest online. Also available in Spanish and as a bilingual group.
publico: Mexican people returning from the United States, and their families, who prefer English or are more comfortable in English (for example, people who grew up in the U.S.).
formato: Hybrid: 1 in-person session of 3 hours and 2 hours online (5 hours total).

personajes.Don Rafa: 52 years old. Worked 18 years in construction in Texas. Deported in March; went back to Michoacán.
personajes.Lupita: 38 years old. Returned by her own decision to Guanajuato with two U.S.-born children.
personajes.Memo: 24 years old. Arrived in the U.S. at age 6; returned to Puebla and barely knows Mexico.
personajes.Chayo: 45 years old. Lives in Oaxaca; received remittances from her husband, who just returned.

problema: They arrive without their papers at hand, or with U.S. papers that can't be used here to open an account.
Their U.S. credit history doesn't count in Mexico, and they're targeted by expensive «no credit check» loans.
They leave wages, accounts, tax refunds and retirement savings in the U.S. without knowing how to recover them.
They don't know whether they have an Afore or how many weeks they contributed before leaving.
In the first months little money comes in, and savings go to family obligations and loans.
Fake fixers, fraud and extortion target people who have just returned.
